outline.chapter_title: Chapter 1: The Challenge of Scaling Context Windows in Large Language Models
outline.description: Introduces the fundamental limitations of current Large Language Models (LLMs) regarding context window size, defines the specific problems encountered when extending beyond standard limits (e.g., 4k to >1M tokens), and reviews existing baseline methods like Linear Interpolation (PI), NTK-aware scaling, and YaRN.
subtopics: The role of context windows in modern LLM applications (agents, RAG, long-document QA)
The 'Out-of-Distribution' problem: Catastrophic values at new token positions
Resource constraints: Scarcity of ultra-long training data and computational costs
Attention dispersion and performance degradation on short contexts
Overview of Positional Encoding: Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE) basics
Limitations of Linear Positional Interpolation (PI)
Review of NTK-based interpolation and YaRN strategies

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 2: Uncovering Non-Uniformities in Positional Information
outline.description: Explores the core theoretical contribution of LongRoPE: the discovery that positional information is not uniform across dimensions or token positions. This chapter details empirical evidence showing why one-size-fits-all interpolation fails and establishes the need for a multi-dimensional, adaptive approach.
subtopics: Empirical analysis of RoPE dimension sensitivity
Finding 1: Dimension-specific non-uniformity (High-frequency vs. Low-frequency dimensions)
Finding 2: Token-position non-uniformity (The importance of initial tokens/streaming effects)
Why current heuristics (like YaRN's grouping) are sub-optimal
Theoretical implications: Minimizing information loss during interpolation
Quantifying the gap between linear/non-uniform methods without fine-tuning

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 3: Methodology I – Evolutionary Search for Optimal Rescaling
outline.description: Details the mathematical formulation of the LongRoPE problem and introduces the custom evolutionary search algorithm designed to navigate the massive combinatorial space of possible rescale factors efficiently.
subtopics: Mathematical formulation: Defining rescale factors ($\lambda_i$) and position thresholds ($\hat{n}$)
Defining the search space bounds and granularity
Evolutionary Algorithms refresher: Population, Mutation, Crossover, Selection
Optimization Technique 1: Warm-starting with PI, NTK, and YaRN populations
Optimization Technique 2: Monotonically non-decreasing constraint based on NTK theory
Algorithm walkthrough: Step-by-step execution of the search process
Efficiency metrics: Reducing perplexity computation costs
